sections.heading: The school calendar Sion families plan around
paragraphs: IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page; schools appear here because their calendars set the dates families work around. Children in Sion are spread across several international schools rather than concentrated in one. Don Bosco International School in Matunga is the closest, a short run north-west from most Sion addresses. Witty International School's Chembur campus is reached down the Sion–Trombay Road or across the SCLR, which is the same corridor the tutors use.

The Mumbai international school year opens in the first half of June, and that start lands inside the monsoon, which matters more at this address than it does in Bandra. By late August the first MYP summative tasks are graded and the first awkward conversation about criterion scores happens. October and November bring IGCSE coursework deadlines and the Year 11 mock series. January and February are the DP1 Internal Assessment proposal months and the DP2 mock exams, often in the same fortnight. March and April are the real squeeze, with the IGCSE May/June series and the DP May session starting while the Extended Essay is already in and TOK essays are done.

Put a real child into that calendar. A DP2 candidate living near Sion Circle, sitting May exams, has her Economics HL Paper 3 practice competing with a TOK exhibition commentary and a school mock timetable that will not move. Her tutor holds a ninety-minute Wednesday slot and nothing else, so the two of them spend February on Paper 3 technique and shift content revision to a Saturday double. That sequencing decision is worth more than an extra hour a week, and it only exists because the slot was booked in November rather than in February, when every capable tutor in Mumbai is already committed.

So we ask which school and which year group before we ask about subjects. A tutor who already works with children at the same school knows when its internal deadlines fall, knows which textbook and syllabus year is in use, and does not spend three sessions working it out. Families at Don Bosco International School and at Witty International School are not on identical calendars, and the difference shows up in November when one set of deadlines arrives a fortnight ahead of the other.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a Sion address?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and should be. A tutor at your dining table sees the actual notebook, the actual school worksheet and the actual mess in the filing, and a DP2 student loses no time to the road in a week with three deadlines. Online is the right second choice rather than a cheaper substitute, and hybrid is where most Diploma families end up.

Most families who ask for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sion want the same arrangement: a fixed weekday evening, the same room every week, and a parent within earshot without sitting in the session. Home classes also solve the sibling case, since all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Sion families run back to back on a Saturday morning cost one travel trip instead of two. The honest price of home tuition is travel: a tutor who gives up ninety minutes of an evening to the road accounts for that, and a session lost to a flooded Tuesday is lost rather than rescheduled.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Sion is the sensible answer in three situations. The first is scarcity: Computer Science HL, Visual Arts, French B or Economics HL sometimes has no free specialist within reach, and an online specialist from elsewhere in Mumbai or outside it beats a nearby generalist every time. The second is monsoon weeks, when the underpass is standing water and nobody is driving. The third is the short, frequent session: a thirty-minute paper review two days before a test does not justify a car journey in either direction.

Hybrid works when the split is deliberate. Put the long session at home on the weekend for IA work, drafting and anything involving diagrams, and a short online session midweek for marking, doubts and timed questions. The trade-offs deserve saying plainly: online needs a quiet room, a stable connection and some way for the tutor to see handwritten working, usually a phone on a stand pointed at the page. It also needs a parent to hold the line, because an online slot is the first thing a tired fifteen-year-old tries to skip.

sections.heading: How is an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sion checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Before any IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sion is put in front of a parent, we verify identity, confirm the qualifications claimed and test board experience by asking for specifics: which syllabus code, which assessment session, which Internal Assessments supervised, which papers marked. A general claim to teach the IB does not survive that conversation.

The subject-code question does most of the work. A tutor who has genuinely taught IGCSE Chemistry can tell you it is 0620, say what changed in the current syllabus and name the paper their students lose marks on. A tutor who has supervised Diploma Internal Assessments can say where candidates fall down on the rubric, and knows the academic-honesty line: a tutor may teach the skill, interrogate a research question and challenge a draft, but the IA must be the candidate's own work. Anyone offering to write or heavily rewrite an IA is a risk to the Diploma, not a shortcut through it.

Then there is what you check yourself, in the first session, in your own home. Put one of your child's recently marked answers in front of the tutor and ask them to mark it again and explain the difference. Ask what the command term evaluate requires that explain does not. Ask how they would structure the next four weeks. Ask what they will send you after each session. Parents ask us who the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Sion is, and the honest answer is that there is no single best tutor, only the one whose explanation your child follows.

We also check the dull things that decide whether an arrangement survives a term: whether the tutor can hold your window every week from their own address, whether they have worked a Sion address before and know the junction, and whether they already carry two other evening slots that will start eating into yours in February. Searches as blunt as IB and IGCSE tutors near me Sion are usually about travel reliability rather than teaching quality, and that is a reasonable thing to care about first.
bullets: Identity and qualification claims verified before a name reaches you.
Board experience tested by syllabus code, session and IAs supervised.
A tutor may challenge an IA draft; writing it breaches academic honesty.
Ask the tutor to re-mark one of your child's own marked answers.
Confirm the tutor can hold your weekly window from their own address.

sections.heading: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Sion actually depend on?
paragraphs: IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Sion depend on five things: the board and level, how scarce the subject specialist is, how far and in which direction the tutor travels, how long and how often sessions run, and whether marking between sessions is included. We do not print a figure on a web page, because any figure printed here would be wrong for half the people reading it.

Board and level is the first lever. IGCSE Core work sits below IGCSE Extended, which sits below Standard Level, which sits below Higher Level, and DP2 exam-year work with Internal Assessment supervision sits above all of it because the tutor is carrying deadlines and risk as well as content. Scarcity is the second lever and sharper than parents expect. Mathematics and English specialists are available across Mumbai. Economics HL, Computer Science, Psychology, Visual Arts, French B and Business Management draw on far thinner pools, and a thin pool sets its own rate regardless of where you live.

Travel is where this address is genuinely better off, and it is the part worth understanding properly. A tutor prices an evening, not an hour. A southern address that takes fifty minutes to reach through the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals consumes most of a tutor's evening for one session, and that shows up in what they will accept. A Sion address reached in under half an hour on the SCLR from Chembur, or in ten minutes from Matunga or Wadala, consumes far less of it. Sitting on the seam between two tutor pools means you are rarely bidding against scarcity and distance at the same time, which is the combination that makes a thin HL subject expensive elsewhere on the island.

Session length and frequency are the levers you control. One weekly ninety-minute slot on a single subject works out differently from two short sessions across two subjects, and asking a tutor to mark a full past paper between visits is extra work that should be agreed rather than assumed. So ask four things before committing: what a session includes, what marking between sessions costs, what happens to a session you cancel on the day, and whether the rate changes in the exam term. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Sion families keep across two years will answer all four without hedging.
bullets: Board and level: Core, Extended, SL, HL and exam-year DP all differ.
Scarce subjects set their own rate wherever in Mumbai you live.
Tutors price the evening, not the hour, so travel direction matters.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one Mumbai exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at a grade. You should be looking for four things: a written diagnosis naming the specific gaps, homework being done without a parent chasing it, your child using command terms correctly in ordinary conversation, and a tutor who can say what the next four weeks will cover and why. If none of that exists after four sessions, the match is wrong, and the fix is a different tutor rather than more hours.

At one term, expect movement in the mechanics before movement in the report. Timed questions get finished. Working gets shown. An MYP criterion score moves because the child finally writes to the strand instead of around it. A single internal grade band is a realistic term's gain for a student who was underperforming their own understanding; two bands happens, but it is not something we promise. We do not guarantee grades, and any tutor or platform in Mumbai that does is selling you something other than tuition.

Across a full exam cycle the gains are structural. A DP2 who started in DP1 has an IA submitted on time rather than in a panic, has sat each paper under timing several times, and knows mark-scheme language well enough to self-mark honestly. A student who starts in February of the exam year gets something narrower and should be told so plainly: triage, the highest-yield topics, paper technique and timing. That is worth doing, and it is a different product from two years of teaching. Being honest about the ceiling at the start is what keeps the arrangement intact after results.

When a tutor is not working out, the useful signal is not a bad week; it is three sessions with no change in what your child can do unprompted. Tell us early. We ask what specifically is not working, because sometimes the answer is the slot rather than the person: a 7pm start after a late school bus fails for reasons nobody in the room can teach their way out of. If it is the person, we move to the next name on the original shortlist, so you are not restarting from zero in the middle of a term.
bullets: Four weeks: a written diagnosis, homework done unchased, command terms used correctly.
One term: timed questions finished, working shown, one realistic grade band.
One exam cycle: IA submitted on time and dependable paper timing.

sections.heading: Starting home classes in Sion: what to have ready
paragraphs: Four things make the first week of IB and IGCSE home classes in Sion useful rather than exploratory. The last report card or grade summary, with the criterion or component breakdown if the school provides one. Two or three pieces of recently marked work, including something the child did badly on. The school's assessment calendar for the term. And a decision about where the session happens: a table, a chair for the tutor, and a room with a door that shuts.

Then sort the gate. Most addresses here are co-operative housing societies around the Circle and the Matunga side, and most want a visitor entry written out every single visit. Ask the secretary or the watchman to record a standing weekly entry for a named tutor at a fixed time, and share the tutor's name and phone number in advance. A tutor arguing at the gate at 6.25pm on a Tuesday loses the first ten minutes of a session you paid for, and it will happen every week until somebody fixes it once.

The first session is diagnostic and should look like it. The tutor works through recent marked material, asks the child to attempt two or three questions unaided, and finds out what is actually missing, which in Mumbai is very often a Year 9 foundation sitting under a Year 11 syllabus. You get a short written note afterwards: what was tested, what was missing, what the next four weeks will cover. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents can book once and keep is realistic at MYP level and much less realistic at Diploma level, where you want specialists per subject.

After that, protect the slot. The families who get the most out of home tuition across Sion, Matunga, Wadala and Kurla are not the ones booking the most hours; they are the ones whose Tuesday at 6.30pm has survived since June. Tell the tutor about school trips and exam weeks in advance, and expect the same courtesy on the evening the SCLR fails them.
bullets: Bring the last report card with its criterion or component breakdown.
Bring two or three recently marked papers, including a bad one.
Fix the room: a table, a chair and a door that shuts.
Register a standing weekly society entry for the named tutor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor from Chembur or Powai really reach Sion for a 6.30pm session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single most useful fact about tuition at this address. Sion is the junction for the Santacruz–Chembur Link Road, so a tutor living in Chembur, Chandivali or Powai covers the distance in under half an hour, which is unusual for an address this close to the island city. The direction of flow helps, because the heavy evening movement is outbound towards the suburbs and an inbound run is lighter. The caveats are the Kurla-end bottleneck and the Sion Circle approach, which is why tutors here commit to a ten-minute arrival window rather than an exact minute.

faqs.question: How quickly can home tuition start once we send our details?
faqs.answer: Usually within a week for common subjects, and longer in February. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Sion is quicker to arrange than most South Mumbai addresses because the shortlist draws on both the island pool and the eastern suburbs across the SCLR. For Mathematics, the sciences, English and MYP support we can normally offer names within two or three days and start the following week. For a thin Higher Level subject in the middle of the exam term, be ready for either a wait, an online tutor, or a weekend slot instead of the weekday evening you wanted.

faqs.question: What do fees for an IB or IGCSE tutor here depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, travel and session structure, in roughly that order. We do not publish a price list because the honest answer varies: IGCSE Core support and DP2 Higher Level work with Internal Assessment supervision are different jobs with different risk. Scarce subjects set their own rate anywhere in Mumbai. Travel is the factor this address is lucky on, since a tutor reaching you across the SCLR or from Matunga spends far less of their evening on the road than one crawling down Peddar Road. Ask what a session includes, what marking costs, and whether exam-term rates change.

faqs.question: Our society issues a visitor pass every single visit. How do we handle a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Register a standing weekly entry instead of relying on the gate each time. Give the society office the tutor's full name, phone number, the day and the time, and ask for it to be recorded as a recurring visit for the term. Share the tutor's number with the watchman on duty that evening as well, because the register and the man at the gate are not always the same system. Without this, a tutor spends the first ten minutes of a paid session on the phone from the gate, and around Sion Circle that repeats every week until someone fixes it.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for a subject with heavy diagrams and written working?
faqs.answer: It works if the setup handles handwriting, and fails badly if it does not. The usual failure is a laptop camera pointed at a face while the real work happens on paper out of shot. Fix it with a second device or a phone on a stand aimed at the page, plus a shared document the tutor can write on. For doubt-clearing, mark-scheme walkthroughs and timed-question review, online matches home tuition and costs nothing in travel. For teaching a topic the child has genuinely not understood, a session at the table is still better.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we move to the next name on the original shortlist. We ask one question first: what specifically is not changing? Sometimes the answer points at the slot rather than the tutor, and a 7pm start after a late school bus is a scheduling problem no tutor can teach their way out of. If it is the person, the replacement comes from the shortlist already built for your subject and your approach road, so a handover takes days rather than a fresh search. We would rather change a tutor in week three than lose a term to politeness.

faqs.question: A month of sessions and the report has not moved. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: At four weeks, usually yes. A report reflects assessments set before the tuition started, so the honest early indicators are different ones: homework being done without chasing, timed questions being finished, correct use of command terms, and a tutor who can name the gaps in writing. What is not normal is four weeks with no written diagnosis and no plan for the next four. If your child still cannot do unprompted what the tutor covered last week, that is the signal to change. We do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor in Mumbai will either.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover every subject for two children in the same evening?
faqs.answer: At MYP and IGCSE level often yes; at Diploma level rarely. Back-to-back slots work well for siblings and save a travel trip, which is why they are among the most durable arrangements a family can book. A capable MYP generalist can hold Sciences and Individuals and Societies for a Year 3 and Year 5 pair without strain. At Diploma level, Higher Level subjects need specialists who have marked that paper, so two children in DP2 usually means two tutors, sometimes on different days of the week.

faqs.question: What happens to home sessions when Gandhi Market and the underpass flood in July?
faqs.answer: Agree the fallback in June, before you need it. The low ground near Gandhi Market and the Sion rail underpass takes standing water in a heavy spell, and on those evenings no tutor is reaching you from Chembur or anywhere else. The arrangement that works is a standing rule: if the road is out by 4pm, the session runs online at the same time rather than being cancelled. Families who settle this in advance lose almost nothing in July and August. Families who improvise lose two or three sessions, usually in the week before a mock.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: For younger children yes, for a Diploma student not really. At PYP and early MYP an adult in the house matters, both for the child's attention and because you want to hear how the tutor explains things. From IGCSE upwards, a parent sitting in the room usually makes the session worse, because the student stops asking the questions that reveal what they do not know. The workable middle position is a session in a room with the door open, a written note from the tutor afterwards, and a proper conversation with the tutor once a month.

faqs.question: Will the tutor help with the Internal Assessment or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the academic-honesty rules, and a tutor who offers more than that is a liability. A tutor can teach the skills an Internal Assessment needs, pressure-test a research question, explain the rubric strand by strand and ask hard questions about a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it or supply the analysis. Schools and the International Baccalaureate both check authenticity, and a problem there costs far more than a weak IA ever would. Ask a prospective tutor directly how they handle drafts; the answer tells you plenty.

faqs.question: What is the difference between exam-season help and a tutor we keep for two years?
faqs.answer: The difference is what you can reasonably expect from each. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Sion families keep from DP1 through DP2 shapes subject choices, supervises Internal Assessments on the real school calendar and builds paper technique across four terms. Exam-season help is triage: highest-yield topics, past-paper timing and mark-scheme language, starting from wherever the student already is. Both are worth doing. The mistake is booking triage in February and expecting the outcome of two years, which no tutor in Mumbai can deliver.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP and IGCSE: which programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Four different assessment systems run in South Mumbai classrooms. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs to roughly Year 5 and is judged by teachers against learning outcomes with no external paper anywhere. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers Years 6 to 10, eight subject groups, and four published criteria per subject marked on best-fit descriptors. IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, puts the last two school years onto external papers with tiered entry. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year sixth form, with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects plus the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and an Internal Assessment (IA) in every subject.

Which of those a South Mumbai family is living with depends almost entirely on the school. Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Bombay International School at Babulnath and Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo run IGCSE into DP, so a family there crosses one board boundary at the end of Year 10. Activity High School on Peddar Road and Gopi Birla Memorial School in Walkeshwar take students through IGCSE, after which sixth form happens somewhere else: that transfer year, with a new board, new command terms and an EE to start, is one of the two points where families here reach for a tutor. JBCN International School in Parel runs both pathways on one campus.

The practical difference for a tutor is what a mark even means. In MYP there is no percentage to chase: a criterion level is awarded against descriptors, so the work is teaching a child to write the kind of answer a descriptor rewards. In IGCSE the live question is tier. Core entry caps the grade available, Extended opens the top of the scale and carries harder papers, and a Year 9 student parked in Core because of one bad term is a decision worth revisiting with evidence rather than feeling. In DP the subject grade is only part of it: the core, EE and TOK, carries its own points and its own deadlines, and most DP families who call us are behind on the core rather than the subject.

Years 1 to 12 are all workable, but they need genuinely different tutors. A PYP Year 3 reader needs someone patient with phonics and willing to sit on the floor. An MYP Year 8 needs a tutor who can read a criterion rubric out loud and translate it. A DP2 HL student needs somebody who has marked that paper against a markscheme and can say which three mark types are being dropped.
bullets: PYP: teacher-assessed outcomes, no external paper, reading and number sense are the real work
MYP: four criteria per subject, best-fit descriptors, no percentage to chase
IGCSE: Core and Extended tiers, and Core puts a ceiling on the grade
DP: HL and SL subjects plus the EE, TOK and an IA in every subject
Board switch at the end of Year 10 is a predictable pressure point, not a crisis

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended: what the tutor has to know
paragraphs: Covering all IB and IGCSE subjects with a tutor in South Mumbai is not one person doing everything. It is a pool deep enough that the right specialist exists for the subject actually in trouble. At IGCSE that means someone who works from the syllabus by its code and not from a generic textbook: Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 behave differently in the exam room, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 each carry an alternative-to-practical component that quietly costs marks all year, and First Language English 0500 is a different job from a second-language paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifications sit alongside the Cambridge ones in several South Mumbai classrooms, which is why the first question a tutor should ask is which specification and which first examination year.

In DP the subject choice itself is often the problem a parent has not named yet. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics Applications and Interpretation are not a harder and easier version of the same course, and a student who chose on reputation rather than on how she thinks will fight the paper for two years. HL versus SL is a question of depth plus one extra assessed component, not of effort. Economics HL adds a policy paper built on unseen material. English A Language and Literature adds an HL essay on top of the guided analysis and the comparative paper. Science HL adds options content and harder data analysis in Paper 3, and every DP subject carries an IA that is worth a fixed share of the final grade and is due when everything else is also due.

Here is what useful subject help looks like in practice. A DP2 Chemistry HL student at a Cuffe Parade school who says her Paper 2 is weak usually does not have a chemistry problem. She has a multi-step equilibrium problem and a command-term problem: she explains where the markscheme wanted her to deduce, and she loses the second and third marks of four-mark questions while getting the first every time. A tutor who takes her last Paper 2, marks it against the published markscheme in front of her and sorts her lost marks into those two piles has done more in one session than four weeks of re-teaching the topic. The same logic applies to an IGCSE 0580 Extended Paper 4, where the losses cluster in multi-stage problems and in showing method.

IA and EE work needs its own treatment. An IA is assessed on criteria, so a tutor's job is to make the student's own investigation hit those criteria, not to improve the write-up by taking it over. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai who starts editing an IA draft rather than questioning the method is a risk to the student, because academic honesty requirements apply to tutoring help too and schools here ask about it.
bullets: Syllabus code and first examination year checked before the first session, every time
Mathematics 0580 and 0607 taught as the different papers they actually are
Alternative-to-practical papers in 0620, 0625 and 0610 treated as examinable content

sections.heading: Which South Mumbai localities do home tutors cover?
paragraphs: Home tuition runs across the whole island. In the far south that means Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Nariman Point, Marine Drive, Churchgate and Fort. On the western ridge it means Malabar Hill, Walkeshwar, Napean Sea Road, Breach Candy, Cumballa Hill, Kemps Corner, Peddar Road and Altamount Road. Through the middle it means Tardeo, Mahalaxmi, Grant Road and Girgaon. On the eastern side it means Byculla, Mazgaon and Sewri. Further north, still South Mumbai for every practical purpose, it means Parel, Lower Parel, Prabhadevi, Worli, Dadar, Matunga, Sion and Wadala. A parent typing IB and IGCSE tutors near me in South Mumbai is rarely asking about the whole island: she is asking whether anyone good is within twenty minutes of her lane at seven in the evening, and that answer changes pocket by pocket.

The transport map explains the matching. The Western Line terminates at Churchgate and runs back out through Marine Lines, Charni Road, Grant Road and Mumbai Central, which makes Churchgate, Marine Drive and Nariman Point easy for a tutor arriving by train and then walking. The Harbour Line from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus through Dockyard Road to Sewri serves the eastern edge, and Dadar is the one station where the Western and Central lines meet, which is why Dadar and Matunga tutors are the most flexible in Mumbai, Maharashtra for the whole island. Metro Line 3, the Aqua line, links Cuffe Parade to BKC and has made a Colaba or Churchgate evening slot realistic for a tutor who lives on that corridor. The Eastern Freeway brings Wadala and Sewri closer to Fort than the map suggests, and the Coastal Road has shortened the Marine Drive to Worli and Prabhadevi run.

What the map does not fix is the evening choke. Peddar Road and the Haji Ali junction decide whether a Breach Candy or Malabar Hill lesson starts on time, and no amount of planning beats them between half past six and half past eight. So a Walkeshwar family is matched with a tutor who can reach the ridge without crossing that junction, a Lower Parel family is matched along the Parel and Prabhadevi line, and a Cuffe Parade family is matched from Colaba, Fort, Churchgate or the Metro Line 3 corridor rather than from across the city. Where a tutor lives matters more in South Mumbai than almost anywhere else in the city, because the distances are so short that travel time is all signal and no road.

Coverage elsewhere exists and is handled by its own page. The Western Suburbs along the Western Express Highway, Metro Lines 1, 2A and 7 and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link cover Bandra, Khar, Juhu and Andheri. The Central Suburbs take Powai and Ghatkopar off JVLR and the Eastern Express Highway. The Eastern Suburbs cover Chembur and Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines. Navi Mumbai covers Vashi and Nerul off Palm Beach Road and the Atal Setu, and Thane covers Majiwada and Kasarvadavali along Ghodbunder Road. Tutors are matched within a zone because a cross-city weekday evening booking fails by about week six.

sections.heading: How the South Mumbai school calendar sets the pressure points
paragraphs: The year opens in June into the monsoon, which is the worst possible combination for a new tutoring arrangement and the most common month for parents to start one. The first six weeks are settling-in, and the first real assessments land in late July and August. By then a DP1 student at Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo or Bombay International School at Babulnath knows whether the HL choices were right, and that is the honest moment to change course rather than in December. August and September bring Ganesh Chaturthi, and in South Mumbai that is not a notional disruption: the Lalbaug and Girgaon processions and the Girgaon Chowpatty immersions close roads for days and make several evening slots in Parel, Girgaon and Grant Road undeliverable. Those sessions get moved online in advance rather than cancelled on the day.

October and November are the Diwali break, and for DP1 families that break is when the Extended Essay goes from a title to a draft. Students at Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort and B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade usually have an EE supervisor meeting shortly after, so a tutor working through that fortnight is working on research questions and sources, not on exam technique. January is mock season, and the January mocks are the number a South Mumbai sixth form actually uses when it talks to a student about predicted grades. One Sunday in January the Mumbai Marathon closes Marine Drive, Peddar Road and the Sea Link, and every weekend slot in Colaba, Churchgate, Napean Sea Road and Worli moves by a day. It happens annually and it still surprises people.

February is the compression point. DP2 IA final deadlines, the TOK essay, the EE final submission and the last mock feedback arrive within a few weeks of each other, and the Year 10 IGCSE cohort at Activity High School on Peddar Road or Gopi Birla Memorial School in Walkeshwar is sitting its own pre-boards at the same time. Sessions in February stop being general subject help and become triage: what is due first, what carries more weight, what can be submitted good enough. Then May is the DP examination session and the IGCSE May and June series, with an October and November IGCSE series as the resit route. Sixth form admissions interviews for students leaving an IGCSE-only school also fall in this window, which is why a quiet March and April in Walkeshwar or Peddar Road is unusual.

Naming these schools is local context and nothing more. Families in these localities attend them, their calendars set the dates that matter, and a tutor who knows those dates plans backwards from them. IB Gram has no relationship with any of them, is not affiliated with any school named here, and nothing on this page should be read as an endorsement from either side.

August to September: Ganesh Chaturthi road closures in Lalbaug, Girgaon and Parel

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid in South Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and for most South Mumbai families it is the right one. A tutor at your dining table works in your child's actual exercise book, sees the handwriting that is costing method marks, and takes the phone out of the equation for ninety minutes. For Years 1 to 10 the difference is large: a Year 7 student will drift in an online session in a way she will not with an adult sitting beside her. The honest cost is supply. A tutor doing home visits on the island can realistically cover two homes on a weekday evening, not four, so the good tutors sell out their half past four and half past six slots first and the family that insists on a seven forty-five start gets a shorter shortlist. Demand for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in South Mumbai also spikes in January and February, which is the worst time to start looking.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in South Mumbai earns its place in three situations. Scarce HL subjects come first: Higher Level Economics, Psychology, Music, Visual Arts theory, French B and Spanish ab initio have a thin pool of tutors anywhere in the city, and insisting on home visits for those means accepting a weaker subject specialist. Monsoon weeks come second, when a flooded stretch at Hindmata or a waterlogged Sion junction turns a twenty-minute trip into an hour. Late slots come third: a nine o'clock online session exists, while a nine o'clock home visit in Cuffe Parade does not. Online needs a real setup though, which means a laptop rather than a phone, a second screen or a printed past paper so the student can write while seeing the tutor, and a parent who occasionally checks which tab is open.

Hybrid is where most DP families here end up after a term. One home session a week carries the structure and the accountability, and a second online session carries the drilling, the past-paper walkthroughs and the IA screen-share, which is genuinely better online because the document is on screen anyway. In the February crunch almost everything moves online for a fortnight because a student with three deadlines cannot afford a tutor stuck at Haji Ali.

There is a third venue worth knowing about. Several of the newer towers here have study rooms or clubhouse spaces that residents can book, and in Lodha World Towers in Lower Parel, Omkar 1973 in Worli, Raheja Vivarea in Mahalaxmi and Piramal Aranya in Byculla that room is often a better classroom than a flat with the television on and a younger sibling circling. It needs booking a week ahead and a resident present to sign the tutor in, but a quiet table with a whiteboard beats a dining table for a DP2 Physics session.
bullets: Home tuition: best for Years 1 to 10, the child's own exercise book, no screen to hide behind

Online: the honest answer for scarce HL subjects and for monsoon weeks
Online needs a laptop, a printed paper to write on and a parent who looks in
Hybrid: one home session for structure, one online for past papers and IA screen-share
Tower study rooms in Lower Parel, Worli, Mahalaxmi and Byculla beat a busy dining table

sections.heading: How tutors are checked, and what you should check yourself
paragraphs: Verification before a match has four parts. Identity comes first: a government photo ID, matched to the name and photograph on the profile you see. Qualification second: the degree certificate or transcript for the subject being taught, because a commerce graduate teaching DP Physics HL is a problem no amount of enthusiasm fixes. Board experience third, and specifically: which syllabus, which specification, which examination sessions, how many cohorts, and whether that experience is current, since syllabuses change and a tutor who last taught a 2016 specification is teaching from memory. Fourth is a subject task. We ask the tutor to mark a real past-paper answer against the published markscheme, or to break a sample IA down by criterion, because that is the thing an engaged parent cannot easily assess in a first conversation and it separates a subject knower from a subject teacher.

Then there is the part only you can do, and an engaged parent catches more than any screening process. At the first session, look at the ID at your door and check it is the person on the profile. Ask which specification and which first examination year your child is sitting, and listen for whether the answer is specific. Ask for your child's own last test or IA draft to be marked in front of you, criterion by criterion, and see whether the feedback names mark types or just says it needs more detail. Ask what week one will cover and what the tutor expects to be different by week four. Sit in on the first session: a tutor who objects to a parent being in the room for session one is telling you something.

Be sceptical of the things that cannot be verified. Nobody can promise a grade, and an IB and IGCSE private tutor in South Mumbai who opens with a promised score is selling rather than teaching. Treat claimed examiner status, claimed school affiliations and claimed success rates as things to ask evidence for. We do not guarantee grades and we would rather say so in the first conversation than in a refund conversation in May. Equally, be cautious of a tutor who will not put the basics in writing: the slot, the duration, the notice period and what happens when a session is missed by either side.

Keep the paperwork small but real. One written line after each session on what was covered and what the homework is, and a short review at week four. That record is what makes a change of tutor cheap instead of a restart, and it is what lets you tell the difference between a child who is not working and a tutor who is not teaching.
bullets: Government photo ID, matched to the profile photograph you were shown
Degree or transcript in the subject, not a general teaching claim

sections.heading: What does an IB and IGCSE home tutor in South Mumbai cost, and what moves the number?
paragraphs: IB and IGCSE tuition fees in South Mumbai are not one number, and any page quoting you one before knowing the subject is guessing. Five factors move the rate, in roughly this order of weight. Board and level: IGCSE Core sits lowest, IGCSE Extended above it, DP SL above that and DP HL highest, because the preparation behind an HL session is longer than the session. Subject scarcity next, and it is the single biggest swing: Mathematics and the sciences have a deep pool here, while HL Economics, Psychology, Music, Visual Arts theory, French B and a second-language ab initio course have a thin one, and a thin pool prices itself. Session length third: a sixty-minute slot works for an IGCSE top-up and does not work for DP HL problem-solving, where ninety minutes is the floor and two hours is common near deadlines.

Travel is the fourth factor and it is specific to this part of the city. A tutor crossing Peddar Road or the Haji Ali junction at half past six surrenders close to two hours of her evening for a ninety-minute lesson, and that is reflected in what she charges and in whether she will take the booking at all. This is exactly why matching inside the island matters financially and not just logistically: a Prabhadevi tutor teaching a Worli student charges for teaching, while a tutor brought from much further away is partly charging for the Western Express Highway. The fifth factor is timing in the year. January and February are the tightest supply window in South Mumbai, with mocks, IA deadlines and the TOK essay all live, so a family starting in June has a materially better choice of tutor than the same family starting in late January.

A few smaller things move it too. One tutor across several subjects is usually cheaper per hour than three specialists and usually weaker in at least one of them, so the sensible version is one generalist for the MYP years and specialists for DP HL. Two siblings in the same session costs less per child and works only if they are within a year or two and the same board. Frequency matters: twice a week for a term beats four times a week for a fortnight, both for the child and for the bill. Intensive IA or EE blocks near a deadline are priced as intensives. Online sessions normally sit below home sessions for the same tutor because nobody is paying for travel.

What you should ask for before the first session, in writing: the rate, the session length, the frequency, the notice period for cancelling, who absorbs a session the tutor misses, and whether the rate changes for an exam-period intensive. Clarity there prevents the two arguments that actually end tutoring arrangements in April. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in South Mumbai is a term-length commitment or it is not worth starting, so price it as a term rather than as an hour.

Subject scarcity is the biggest single swing, especially in HL humanities and languages

sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks, a working tutoring arrangement has produced a diagnosis and not a grade. By the end of the first month you should be able to name, in one sentence each, the three things your child is actually getting wrong: not that she is weak at Chemistry, but that she cannot handle multi-step equilibrium, she writes describe answers to explain questions, and she skips the method line that carries the mark. You should also see a change in how homework is done, and the tutor should be working from your child's own marked work rather than from a workbook. If week five arrives with no named gaps and no change in routine, the match is wrong and it is cheaper to say so then than in February.

At one term, the numbers should start moving, and they move in internal marks and criterion levels before they move anywhere official. An MYP student should be gaining a level in the criterion that was targeted, not across all four at once. An IGCSE student should be improving on identifiable paper sections in school tests. A DP student should have an IA draft that exists on time and a mock that is better on the specific papers the tutor worked on. Term two is also when a tier or level decision should be revisited with evidence: a Year 9 student entered for Core who is now consistently handling Extended material has a case, and that case has to be made to the school with marked work behind it.

A full exam cycle is the honest window for a grade to change, and it is worth saying plainly because the alternative is a disappointed family in July. A student who starts in June with a term and a half before mocks has time. A DP2 student who starts in February with three HL subjects behind has triage, which is real and useful and not the same thing as a transformation. We do not guarantee grades and no tutor can, because attendance, homework between sessions, the school's own teaching and what the student does in the exam room all sit outside a tutor's control. What a good tutor reliably changes is clarity about what is wrong and the technique to fix it.

When it is not working, the fix is fast and unglamorous. Tell us after the first or second session, not at the end of the term, and say what specifically is off: the subject depth, the pace, the explaining style, the timekeeping. We re-match from the same subject pool, the new tutor gets the handover notes and the diagnosis already done, and the weekly slot and building arrangement stay as they are. Changing tutors twice in a term is a signal worth pausing on, and usually means the original brief was wrong rather than the tutors.
bullets: Week four: three named gaps in plain language, and homework being done differently
Week four is not when a grade moves, and anyone promising that is guessing
One term: criterion levels and internal marks moving on the targeted areas

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in South Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Six things make the first session worth paying for instead of a get-to-know-you chat. The last report card or progress report, with the teacher comments left in. The subject guide or syllabus code, which the school office or the student portal has, so the tutor is working from the right specification. The current IA or coursework task sheet with its internal deadline, if there is one. Two or three recently marked tests or past papers, with the marks and the teacher's annotations still on them. The school's assessment calendar for the term, because planning backwards from real dates is most of what a tutor is for. And honesty about the slot: the evening your family can actually hold every week, not the one that looks good on paper.

Then the building. In most South Mumbai addresses a tutor is a visitor and the gate is the thing that decides whether the first session starts on time. Older buildings in Walkeshwar, Napean Sea Road and Fort often have a single small lift and a register at the door. The towers in Lower Parel, Worli, Mahalaxmi and Byculla run on pre-approved visitor entries, app-based gate passes or a resident's call to security. Either way, the arrangement to make is a standing weekly entry rather than a fresh approval each Thursday, and that is worth sorting in the first week. Tell us the rule at your gate and whether there is parking or whether the tutor should come by train to Churchgate, Grant Road, Dadar or Byculla and walk.

The first session itself should be diagnostic. Expect the tutor to spend the first part of it on your child's own marked work, asking her to talk through how she answered rather than re-teaching the topic, and the rest on one small piece of corrected technique so the session ends with something concrete. Expect a short written note afterwards: what was covered, what the gaps look like, what the homework is and what the next three sessions will target. If that note does not arrive, ask for it, because it is the thing that makes week nine measurable.

One last practical point for a parent in Colaba, Breach Candy, Dadar or anywhere between. Decide now what happens to a missed session, because something will be missed: a monsoon day, a school event, an unwell tutor, a Ganesh Chaturthi road closure in Girgaon. A rule agreed in June costs nothing and a rule argued about in February costs the arrangement. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in South Mumbai is only as useful as the slot you both manage to protect.

faqs.question: How does a home tutor actually reach Cuffe Parade or Colaba for a six-thirty weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Usually by train to Churchgate or Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and then on foot or by taxi, or by road from inside the island. The far south is well served by the Western Line terminus at Churchgate and the Harbour Line, and Metro Line 3 now links Cuffe Parade to the BKC corridor, so a tutor living along either does the trip reliably. What does not work is a tutor driving down from the suburbs in the evening peak. For a six-thirty start we match from Colaba, Fort, Churchgate, Nariman Point or the Metro corridor, and we tell you honestly if your preferred slot only has late options.

faqs.question: Our building in Lower Parel needs a gate pass for every visitor. How does that work for a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: It works best as a standing weekly entry set up once, rather than a fresh approval every week. Towers like the ones in Lower Parel, Worli and Mahalaxmi typically run app-based visitor approvals or a resident call to security, so you pre-approve the tutor for a fixed day and time and security has the name on file. Older buildings in Walkeshwar or Fort usually want a signature in a register and an ID shown at the door. Tell us your building's rule when you book and we brief the tutor before the first visit, including whether to expect a service lift or a wait at the gate.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in South Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level, subject scarcity, session length, travel and the time of year. IGCSE Core sits lowest and DP HL highest, because HL preparation takes longer than the lesson. Scarce subjects such as HL Economics, Psychology, Music or a second-language ab initio course cost more simply because fewer tutors here teach them. A ninety-minute session costs more than sixty and is the realistic minimum for HL problem-solving. An evening crossing of Peddar Road or Haji Ali is paid for in the tutor's time. And January to February is the tightest supply window, so starting in June gets you more choice at a better rate.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all IB and IGCSE subjects, or do we need several?
faqs.answer: One tutor for the primary and middle years, specialists from DP onwards. Through PYP and the early MYP a single good tutor can genuinely hold Maths, Science and English together, and the consistency helps a younger child more than subject specialism does. From IGCSE Extended and especially in DP HL that stops being true: HL Chemistry and HL Economics are different professions, and a generalist will be visibly out of depth in at least one of them by the second month. Most South Mumbai families we work with end up with one tutor for the younger child and one per difficult subject for the DP student.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring really as good as home tuition for DP Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: For DP HL it is often equal and sometimes better, which is not true lower down. HL work is past papers, markschemes and IA documents, all of which live on a screen anyway, so a screen-share session loses very little. What online does lose is the accountability of an adult in the room, which matters far more for a Year 7 student than for a DP2 student with an exam date. The practical argument for online in HL is access: it opens up the strongest subject specialist rather than the strongest one willing to cross Peddar Road at seven in the evening.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after two sessions. What happens next?
faqs.answer: You tell us what is specifically wrong and we re-match, usually within the same week. Say whether it is subject depth, pace, explaining style or timekeeping, because that determines who replaces them. The new tutor gets the handover notes and the diagnosis already done, so the first session is not spent repeating the assessment, and your weekly slot and gate arrangement stay unchanged. Two sessions is the right point to raise it: waiting a full term wastes the term. If a second match also fails, we go back to the original brief, which is usually where the mistake was.

faqs.question: We are on Malabar Hill and our child is at Cathedral and John Connon School. Will a tutor know that school's calendar?
faqs.answer: A tutor working in South Mumbai will know the rhythm, and we send the specifics anyway. The pattern is familiar across the island schools: first assessments in late July and August, the Extended Essay draft over the Diwali break, mocks in January, and IA, TOK and EE deadlines compressed into February. Your school's own dates come from you or the student portal, and the tutor plans backwards from them. One thing to be clear about: IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with Cathedral and John Connon School or any other school named here, and naming a school is local context rather than any form of endorsement.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: No change in grades after a month is normal; no change in clarity is not. By week four you should be able to name the three specific things going wrong, and your child should be doing homework differently. What you should not expect at four weeks is a moved grade, because school assessments are spaced out and technique takes a cycle to show up in marks. If week five has no named gaps, no work on your child's own marked papers and no written session notes, that is a match problem rather than a patience problem, and you should ask for a change.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Someone should be in the flat, though not in the room after the first session. For the first session we recommend you sit in: it is the fastest way to judge whether the tutor explains or just knows. After that, an adult at home is mainly a safeguarding and practical matter, and most South Mumbai families have help at home who can let the tutor in and sign them at the gate. What matters more than supervision is the study space: a table away from the television, decent light, and a younger sibling kept out for ninety minutes.

faqs.question: What happens if a session is missed because of monsoon flooding near Hindmata or Sion?
faqs.answer: It moves online the same evening if possible, and is rescheduled if not. Monsoon disruption at Hindmata, the Sion junction or a waterlogged stretch of the Eastern Freeway is predictable enough that we ask families to agree a rule in the first week: a flooded evening converts to an online session at the same time, and a genuinely lost session is made up within the fortnight. Agreeing that in June removes the argument in July. During heavy weeks some South Mumbai families move both weekly sessions online until the worst of it passes, which is usually the right call for a DP2 student with deadlines.

faqs.question: Should we start IGCSE support in Year 9 or wait until Year 10?
faqs.answer: Year 9 is the better answer, and the reason is tier entry. Core and Extended decisions are often made during Year 9 on the evidence of that year's work, and Core caps the grade a student can be awarded, so a child who is capable of Extended but having a rough Year 9 can be placed below her ceiling for reasons that have nothing to do with ability. Starting in Year 9 also means the first real syllabus content is being learned properly rather than repaired. A Year 10 start is still worth doing, but it is repair work with a deadline attached.

faqs.question: Do you take on a DP2 student in January, or is that too late?
faqs.answer: We do, with a clear agreement about what January can achieve. A DP2 student starting in January has mocks, IA deadlines, the TOK essay and the EE final submission inside a few weeks, so the first job is triage: what is due first, what carries more weight, what can be submitted at good enough rather than perfect. That is genuinely useful work and it often rescues the core points. What it is not is a path to a transformed subject grade, and we would rather say that in the first call. Earlier is always better, which is why we push June starts.

ssc-to-igcse-transition.heroIntro: Parents planning an SSC to IGCSE transition in Mumbai are rarely worried about the syllabus. They are worried their child will be a year behind. This page gives the honest diagnosis: which SSC habits transfer, which ones start costing marks under the new board, and what IGCSE home tuition should actually do in the first month.
