sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for an Ulwe family: what actually holds?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and it is the right default. A tutor at your table in Ulwe sees what a video call hides: the phone face-up beside the notebook, the diagram redrawn three times, the past paper never attempted because the student could not start question one. For an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Ulwe the practical shape is a 90-minute weekday evening session from 6pm, or a two-hour weekend morning block, which is the better of the two for anything involving an Internal Assessment.

Online earns its place for scarce subjects and for the midweek check. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Ulwe is often the only realistic option for Theory of Knowledge, Psychology, Economics at Higher Level, French B or Visual Arts, because the teaching population for those subjects sits near the older international schools in South Mumbai and the Western Suburbs. Online also survives the monsoon week when nothing moves on the Sion-Panvel Highway, and it suits a 30-minute draft review that is not worth anybody's drive in either direction.

Hybrid is what most Ulwe families settle into by the second month, usually without planning it. One home session at the weekend for the teaching that needs paper, a table and a tutor watching the working, plus one or two shorter online sessions midweek for marking, question practice and keeping a deadline honest. Covering all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes in Ulwe is rarely the plan; covering the subject that is slipping at home, and the rest online when something is due, usually is. The trade-offs run both ways: home sessions carry travel time that is priced in and fail quietly when the only space is a living room with the television on, while online sessions need a tablet and stylus for anything with working and a parent walking past occasionally.

sections.heading: What is checked before a home tutor reaches your door in Ulwe
paragraphs: Before an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Ulwe is offered a slot, the checks are documentary and specific. Government photo identity. The degree or teaching qualification claimed, seen as a document rather than described in a sentence. Evidence of having taught the exact syllabus, which for these boards means naming the subject code and the version of the subject guide, and in practice means being able to say what changed in the current version. At least one reference from a family or a school who worked with them recently.

The trial session does the rest of the work, because paperwork cannot show whether somebody can hold a 15-year-old's attention at 7pm. Afterwards we ask the parent three things: did the tutor know the syllabus, did the child talk, and did the hour have a plan. A tutor who spent the session demonstrating how elegant their own method is, while the child watched politely, is the wrong tutor whatever the credentials say.

Some checks only a parent can run, and in Ulwe one of them is travel. Ask how the tutor will get here and what time they leave. A tutor driving from Kharghar has an easy answer. A tutor crossing the Atal Setu for a weekday evening should be asked directly what their return leg looks like at 8:30pm, because that answer predicts whether the arrangement survives to December. Ask also for a marked sample of the component your child is working on, with the criteria visible on it. None of this is background-check theatre. It filters the two failures that actually happen: a tutor who knows the subject but not the assessment, and a tutor whose commute makes them unreliable by week six. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Ulwe who clears both tends to stay.

sections.heading: What the Atal Setu changes, and what it does not, for tutoring in Ulwe
paragraphs: The Atal Setu, formally the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, lands on this side of the water at Chirle, minutes from Ulwe, and runs across to Sewri in Mumbai, Maharashtra. Off-peak it puts South Mumbai around twenty minutes away by car, which is less than the drive from Ulwe to Thane and less than many crosstown trips inside the suburbs. For tutoring that is not a minor convenience. It is the one piece of infrastructure on this side of the city that genuinely changed which tutors can be offered to a family, and Ulwe, sitting at the Navi Mumbai end of it, is the address where the change is largest.

What it changes is specific, so be specific about it. A Saturday 10:30am session at a home in Ulwe is now genuinely available to a tutor living in Wadala, Sewri, Parel or Worli: they leave at a quarter to ten, they are back by two, and the bridge is clear in both directions. A Tuesday 6pm session is a different proposition entirely. The tutor drives out against the evening flow, finishes at half past seven, and then returns into the island city's own peak, with a toll each way and no rail fallback, because Bamandongri and Targhar sit on the Uran corridor rather than on anything heading towards Churchgate. The bridge added weekend and daytime capacity. It did not add weekday evening capacity, and a page that tells you otherwise is selling something.

The second honesty is that a South Mumbai tutor still has to want the trip. They will want a two-hour block rather than a 55-minute slot, a fixed weekly time rather than one that drifts, and often a stacked morning, teaching one family in Ulwe and another in Kharghar or Panvel before heading back. A household that asks for Saturday 11am and protects it will keep that tutor for a year. A household that reschedules twice loses them by the third month, and no amount of new road surface changes that arithmetic.

Here is the shape that works, taken from the component Ulwe has least local supply for. A DP1 student at D.Y. Patil International School is preparing the English A: Language and Literature Individual Oral, the ten-minute presentation plus five minutes of questions, built on a global issue with one literary extract paired against one non-literary text. Saturday 10:30, two hours of home tuition in Ulwe with a tutor who drove the bridge: they settle the global issue, choose the extract pair and build the structure, which is the part that needs two people and a table. Midweek, two forty-minute online sessions review her recorded run-throughs against the four criteria, knowledge and understanding, analysis and evaluation, focus and organisation, and language. A second Saturday at home is a full timed run with the tutor in the room. That is four contact points in a fortnight, two drives in total, and a component that would otherwise have been prepared entirely over video by somebody who never met her.

sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks, one term and one exam series in Ulwe
paragraphs: Four weeks is a process checkpoint, not a marks checkpoint. By the fourth session the tutor should have found the real gap, which is often two years upstream of the current topic: a DP1 Physics student stuck on kinematics graphs usually has an older problem reading gradients. What you should see at home is a child who starts questions instead of staring at them, shows working without being told to, and can say aloud what a question is asking before attempting it. Those three are the leading indicators. Marks are the lagging one.

One term is where marks should move, and where you should expect specifics rather than impressions. Ask the tutor for evidence: which internal test, which paper, which criterion. In an MYP subject that means a criterion score that shifted and the descriptor explaining why. In IGCSE it means marks recovered on the structured questions rather than a general sense of improvement. In DP it means an IA draft with a justified method section instead of a described one. A tutor who cannot point at a specific piece of work after a term has not been teaching to the assessment, and that is worth raising directly rather than waiting.

One exam series is the real test and it rarely draws a straight line. Students who move up a band usually do it in one step, after something clicks, not by gaining a fraction each month, so a flat term in the middle of an upward year is normal and is not by itself a reason to change anyone. What none of this comes with is a promised outcome. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and any tutor who does should be asked how, because the final mark depends on a student, an examiner and a syllabus that none of us control. What a working arrangement in Ulwe does produce is a visible chain: a plan, work marked against published criteria, and a parent who can name which component improved and which still has not.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Ulwe: what to have ready
paragraphs: Everything needed to start IB and IGCSE home tuition in Ulwe fits on one page. The board and programme, the subject and level, the school and year group, the most recent report card or internal test with the teacher comments left intact, the current subject guide if the school has shared it, and the brief for any Internal Assessment already issued. Add the two slots you can realistically protect each week and whether you want the tutor at your flat, online, or a mix of the two.

The first session is diagnostic and should look like it. Expect the tutor to spend the opening twenty minutes on recent work rather than teaching: the last test, the questions that were skipped, the IA brief, the topics the student says they do not understand and the ones they wrongly believe they do. Expect a short written plan at the end naming the next three sessions and the component each one targets. A first session that was a lecture is a warning sign worth acting on in the same week.

After that the rhythm is yours to hold. Keep the slot on the same day and time, because the family that protects the slot is the family that gets a full year out of the tutor, and that matters most when the tutor is driving the Atal Setu from the island city for it. Tell us at week four how it is going, in one honest sentence. If the answer is lukewarm we shortlist again from the brief already on file, and the second match is normally quicker because the hard information, the school calendar, the slot and the subject, is already recorded.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Ulwe depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and none of them is a fixed rate card. Board and level, since Higher Level DP work costs more per hour than MYP support. faqs.question: How do I judge the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Ulwe?
faqs.answer: Judge the fit rather than the label, because nobody can hand you an objective ranking. Three questions separate tutors quickly: which version of the subject guide are you teaching from, can I see something you have marked against the published criteria, and what will the first four weeks cover. A tutor who answers all three concretely is better for your child than one with a longer list of school names. Then watch the trial session itself. By the second half the child should be doing most of the talking and most of the writing, and the tutor should be mostly asking questions.

faqs.question: Our building is still filling up and has no study room. Where should sessions happen?
faqs.answer: Use the dining table, and clear it before the tutor arrives. Ulwe's housing stock is new, many towers are only partly occupied, and the clubhouse or study room shown in the brochure is often not running yet, so the flat is the practical venue for home classes. What matters is a hard surface, a chair at the right height, the television off and the phone in another room. If a younger sibling is at home, a bedroom with the door open usually works better than a shared living area. Tell us the setup before the first visit and the tutor will plan around it.

faqs.question: My child travels to D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. When should we schedule sessions?
faqs.answer: Weekdays from 6pm and weekends from 10am. The Nerul commute up Palm Beach Road takes a real bite out of the afternoon, and a child who has been on a bus since 3:45pm will not absorb a Chemistry paper at 5pm. Weekend mornings are the most productive hours available to Ulwe families and should carry the heavy work, which usually means the Internal Assessment or the subject the child avoids. Keep the midweek session short and specific: one past paper section, or one draft reviewed against its criteria, not a general revision hour.

faqs.question: Does an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Ulwe work as well for Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: For most Higher Level content, yes, with two conditions. The student needs a tablet and stylus or a second camera so the tutor sees working as it happens rather than a photograph of it afterwards. And the student needs to be old enough not to drift, which in practice means online suits DP1 and DP2 far better than it suits a Year 9 child. For Higher Level Mathematics and Physics, online plus a fortnightly home session usually beats online alone, because somebody has to watch how a problem is set up, not only what the final answer was.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Four weeks is enough to see process change but often not mark change, so check the right signal. By the fourth session the child should be starting questions without prompting, showing working, and able to say what a question is asking for. If those three are present, marks usually follow within a term. If none of them are present after four sessions, the problem is the match rather than the pace, and we would far rather change the tutor at week four than at week twelve. Tell us what you are seeing and we will ask the tutor for their read the same week.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out. How does a replacement happen?
faqs.answer: Tell us, and we re-shortlist rather than restart. You do not owe anyone an explanation beyond the practical one: the slot keeps moving, the syllabus is not being covered, the child has stopped talking during sessions. Because the original brief, the school calendar and your protected slot are already on file, a replacement profile for Ulwe usually arrives faster than the first one did. We do ask for the reason in a sentence, because the second match is noticeably better when we know what failed in the first, and that is worth the awkward thirty seconds.

faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is usually the wrong goal. Up to MYP Year 8 one strong generalist can hold most of the load. From Year 9 onwards the papers are specialised enough that a Mathematics specialist and a Sciences specialist together beat one person covering both adequately. What most families settle on is one weekly specialist for the subject at risk, a fortnightly session on the second, and a shared deadline calendar for the rest. Ulwe filled up quickly and recently, so unlike Kharghar or Vashi it has not had twenty years to accumulate experienced teachers living a few sectors away. Searches for tutors near me in Ulwe return thin results for that reason, not because nobody will teach here. sections.heading: How IB Gram shortlists an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Vasai
paragraphs: Start with the awkward fact, because every honest shortlist for this belt begins there. Vasai is a forty-minute train ride north of Borivali, so the pool of subject specialists who will commit to a standing 6pm weekday slot here is small, and it narrows again the moment you name a board and a subject. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Vasai who teaches Diploma Programme (DP) Chemistry is not the same search as one who teaches International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) Mathematics, and both take longer to staff than the equivalent request anywhere in Mumbai between Bandra and Borivali.

So the first thing we ask for is not a budget. It is the board, the year group, the exact subjects and levels, the name of the school, and the two weekday evening slots that genuinely work in your house. Two slots, not one: a single immovable 7pm Tuesday request knocks out most of the people who could otherwise help. We also ask what has already been tried, because a family that has cycled through two local tutors needs a different kind of match than one starting fresh.

Then we split the shortlist by mode rather than pretending every name is equally reachable. One group is subject specialists who teach online and have taught your syllabus at your level. A second, smaller group is tutors who live in or near the Vasai-Virar belt and can physically sit at your dining table. We show you both, with what each has actually taught and when they are free, and we say plainly which of them is a weekly proposition and which is a before-exams proposition.

sections.heading: Which programmes and boards a Vasai family is actually choosing between
paragraphs: Most households here are inside one of four assessment systems, and the tutoring you need is different in each. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the early years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) in the middle school, and the Diploma Programme (DP) in the final two years. Alongside it sits IGCSE, offered through Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, typically across Years 9 to 11. A child in Vasai travelling to a school in Dahisar East or Borivali may well pass through two of these in six years, which is more board-switching than a family living inside Mumbai city usually deals with.

The practical consequence is that the word tutor means something different in each band. PYP work is about reading stamina, number sense and the habit of explaining thinking out loud, and it is largely parent-supported with light tutor involvement. MYP introduces criterion-based marking, which is where families first discover that a child who knows the content can still score poorly because the criteria reward a kind of writing nobody taught them. IGCSE is the first terminal-exam system most of these students meet: mark schemes, method marks, and a syllabus you can actually tick off. DP adds Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) decisions, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK), and an Internal Assessment (IA) in almost every subject.

IB Gram staffs all IB and IGCSE subjects across IB and IGCSE Years 1-12 with a tutor Mumbai families can keep for a whole academic year rather than a fortnight. Parents here often ask for one all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Vasai and then discover that the person who is genuinely strong on MYP Individuals and Societies criteria is rarely the same person who is strong on DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL. We would rather tell you that at the shortlist stage than have you find out in February.

If you are still choosing a pathway, the question to ask is not which board is harder. It is which board your child's school actually runs well, how many of your subject choices are offered, and whether the final two years will be taken at the same school. A transfer at the end of Year 10 from an IGCSE stream into a DP cohort is survivable, but it needs a planned summer, not a hopeful one.

sections.heading: What subject choice, HL/SL and Core/Extended decisions mean for home tuition
paragraphs: A request for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Vasai usually resolves into two tutors rather than one, and the split is almost always sciences-and-maths on one side, languages-and-humanities on the other. Before you fix the timetable, settle the structural decisions, because they change who you need. At IGCSE, Mathematics splits into Core and Extended, and the Extended paper pair asks for algebraic fluency the Core pair never tests; moving a child down to Core in Year 11 caps the grade available and can close off DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. At DP, the HL and SL choice is not a difficulty dial. HL adds content, a longer paper, and in several subjects an entirely extra paper.

Each subject also carries its own internal assessment, and those deadlines, not the exams, are what wreck a Vasai term. DP Physics and Chemistry each need an individual investigation. Mathematics needs an exploration. Economics needs commentaries on published articles. English needs oral and written coursework. A DP2 student at a Borivali school will often have two IA deadlines and a TOK essay draft landing inside the same three weeks in the first term, while still commuting across the creek twice a day.

Here is a worked example of a component that is taught genuinely well online, which matters when a weekday home tutor is hard to staff. Take a DP1 student taking Economics SL, with her first IA commentary due. The commentary is short, built on a news article she has chosen, and marked against criteria that reward an accurate diagram, correct terminology, real analysis of the article's situation, and evaluation that weighs the policy rather than listing its pros. In a sixty-minute online session the tutor can open the article in a shared tab, ask her to draw the price-ceiling diagram on a shared whiteboard, and then annotate the three things she has mislabelled in a second colour while she watches. The axes get fixed, the shortage is marked as a quantity gap rather than a price gap, and the evaluation paragraph is rewritten in front of her with the criterion read aloud.

That session loses almost nothing by being on a screen, because the artefact is a document and a diagram. A mechanics problem being set out by hand on paper, or an IGCSE Chemistry practical write-up where the student needs someone to look over her shoulder at a table of results, loses more. Sorting your subjects into those two buckets is the single most useful thing you can do before booking anyone.

sections.heading: Does one tutor really cover Vasai, Virar, Bhayandar and Mira Road?
paragraphs: Sometimes, and only along the line. A tutor based in the Vasai-Virar belt can hold weekly slots in Vasai and Virar comfortably, and can usually stretch south to Nalasopara or Naigaon. Bhayandar and Mira Road sit on the far side of Vasai Creek, which is a real water boundary and not a notional one, so a tutor crossing it for a single sixty-minute lesson rarely keeps it up past the second month.

Vasai Road is the station everything here is measured from, and it is where tutors either arrive or decide not to. The Western Line runs north to south from Churchgate up through Bandra, Andheri, Borivali and Dahisar, then crosses the creek to Naigaon, Vasai Road, Nalasopara and Virar. Searching for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Vasai returns results from all of that, which is why a shortlist that does not state travel time is worthless. The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, and a tutor going from Bandra to Andheri is quick off-peak and painful at 6pm. Matching along the line, Khar to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali, works far better than matching across it, and the same logic places an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Vasai from somewhere in the same belt rather than somewhere in the Central Suburbs.

There is a second thing worth saying out loud, because it shapes expectations. Vasai is administratively outside Mumbai city: it is governed by its own municipal corporation in Palghar district, inside the wider metropolitan region of Mumbai, Maharashtra, rather than by the city corporation that covers Dahisar and everything south of it. It has the feel of a town with its own centre, its own market streets and its own quieter evenings, not the feel of a suburb that happens to be far out. Tutors who have only worked between Bandra and Borivali read the map wrong here, assume the last leg is a short autorickshaw, and then discover the distances inside the belt itself.

In practice the belt divides into three workable pockets: Vasai West towards the beach and the older town, Vasai East towards the highway and the industrial stretch, and the Virar side further north. A tutor who lives in one of those pockets is a weekly proposition for that pocket and a fortnightly one for the others. Say which pocket you are in when you send the request; it changes the shortlist more than your budget does.

sections.heading: Which schools do Vasai families travel to, and when does the pressure land?
paragraphs: Mostly south, and that commute is the reason evenings are tight. Families in this belt who want an international curriculum typically travel to Singapore International School in Dahisar East or to JBCN International School, Borivali, both of which sit on the far side of the creek. A child leaving Vasai at seven in the morning and getting home near five has perhaps three usable hours before she is too tired to learn anything, and a tutor arriving at 6pm is competing with that exhaustion. This is a scheduling problem, not a motivation problem, and treating it as the latter is how families lose a term.

The calendar is the other half of it. Both the IB and IGCSE years here run on an academic year that opens around June, so the first term carries the heaviest coursework load: IA drafts, TOK planning, and in DP1 the first real encounter with criterion marking. October and the Diwali break are when families realise a subject has slipped. January and February are mock season for DP2 and for IGCSE candidates sitting the May and June series, and those are also the months when the May IA final deadlines fall. March and April are revision months with very little new teaching in them. An IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai families bring in during February is usually doing damage control rather than teaching.

What this means for a Vasai household is that the useful months to start are June, July and August, when there is room to build a routine, and the expensive months to start are January and February, when there is not. If you are reading this in the first term, you are in the good window. If you are reading it in the week before mocks, the honest answer is to pick one subject and one paper and work on that alone.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with Singapore International School, JBCN International School, Borivali, or any other school named anywhere on this page. Schools appear here only because they set the calendar your family lives by. We have no arrangement with any of them, no access to their internal assessment schedules, and no standing with their teachers.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a family across the creek?
paragraphs: Home tuition first, because it is what most parents here actually want and it remains a real option, particularly for exam season. A tutor in your flat gets things no screen gives: she sees the desk, the lighting, the phone face-down on the bed, the younger sibling in the next room. She can pick up a pencil and write out a method on the student's own paper, and she can tell from posture when the student has stopped following. For paper-heavy work, an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Vasai sitting at your table on a Saturday afternoon will cover more ground in ninety minutes than two online hours would.

The honest problem is supply. A weekday home tutor is genuinely hard to staff in this belt, because the subject specialist who teaches your child's syllabus very likely lives between Andheri and Borivali, and a return trip across the creek on a weekday evening costs her three hours for one lesson. Those arrangements collapse somewhere around week six, usually politely, usually blamed on the trains. That is why most families here begin with an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Vasai and add home sessions when the exam calendar makes them worth the travel.

Online is not a consolation prize, and it is better at some things than home tuition is. It makes the strongest subject specialists reachable regardless of where they live, it survives monsoon weeks and track disruption, it is easier to hold at 8pm after a long commute, and it leaves a record: a shared folder of annotated work, a whiteboard you can scroll back through, a chat log of the questions asked. For essay subjects, data response, Economics commentaries and anything where the artefact is a document, it is close to equivalent.

The arrangement that holds longest in Vasai is a hybrid one that is deliberate rather than accidental. Weekly online lessons with the specialist through the first term, then a block of in-person home classes in the weeks before mocks and again before the final series, with a Saturday slot rather than a weekday evening so travel is survivable. The important part is that the home sessions are scheduled in advance, in writing, at the start of the engagement. A hybrid plan nobody wrote down becomes an online-only plan by December.

sections.heading: How do you vet an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Vasai you will mostly meet on a screen?
paragraphs: By checking documents, teaching history and a sample of real work, in that order, and by refusing to let charm stand in for any of them. Before a tutor reaches a shortlist for an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Vasai request, we verify government photo identity, collect degree and any teaching qualification documents, and record exactly which boards, subjects and levels the person has taught and for how long. We ask for the syllabus codes they work from and the examination series they have prepared students for. A tutor who cannot name the paper structure of the subject they claim to teach does not go on a list.

We then take references from people who have actually seen the teaching, and we ask them narrow questions rather than broad ones: did the tutor turn up, did written feedback arrive, did the student's marks on a specific paper type change, did the tutor say when something was outside her subject. Broad questions produce warm answers. Narrow ones produce useful ones. None of this is an endorsement. IB Gram is a matching platform, and verification establishes that a person is who they say they are and has taught what they say they have taught, nothing more.

The parent's own checks matter more here than anywhere else in Mumbai, because you will mostly meet this person on a screen. Ask to see the tutor's own written solution to a past-paper question your child got wrong, not a generic worked example from a book. Ask what she will send you after each session and insist it is in writing. Ask her to name the syllabus section the lesson belongs to. Ask what she will do in the first fortnight and what she expects to be different by the end of it. Then ask the uncomfortable one: what would make you tell us this is not working?

For IB and IGCSE home tuition in Vasai specifically, add one physical check before exam season. Whatever the mode in term one, arrange one in-person session before the first block of home classes, with you in the flat. It confirms the identity you verified on documents, it lets you see how the person behaves in your house, and it gives the student one face-to-face hour with someone she has only seen in a window. Do this in October or November, not the week before mocks.

sections.heading: The first month: a trial protocol when you cannot meet the tutor in person
paragraphs: This is the section built for Vasai, because the distance means your judgement has to come from evidence instead of impression. Run the first four weeks as a trial with a stated protocol, tell the tutor on day one that you are running it, and write down what you expect to see. Good tutors are relieved by this. The ones who are not have told you something useful for free.

The trial session itself should be on a topic your child is stuck on right now, not a topic the tutor chooses. Pick the last test she did badly on and hand over the paper. Then watch for four things. Does the tutor spend the first ten minutes diagnosing rather than lecturing, asking the student to attempt something so she can see where the understanding breaks? Does she name the syllabus section and the mark scheme, so the work is anchored to the assessment and not to a textbook chapter? Does she make the student do most of the writing? And does she end by setting one specific task for the next forty-eight hours, rather than a vague instruction to revise? A session where your child watched a confident adult solve problems beautifully is a bad session, however much she enjoyed it.

Then require artefacts, because artefacts travel across a creek and impressions do not. Inside the first four weeks you should hold: a short written note after each session saying what was covered, what was weak and what was set; one page listing the topics still to cover with a rough order and dates; at least two pieces of your child's own work marked with mark-scheme or criterion references rather than ticks; and the tutor's own written solution to one past-paper question, so you can see whether she can actually produce the standard she is asking for. Also settle the technical housekeeping in week one: which whiteboard, whether handwriting comes through a tablet or a document camera, who calls back when the connection drops, and whether sessions are recorded.

The four-week checkpoint is a conversation with the plan on the table, and it has three questions. First, can your child name what she is working on this week and why, without looking it up? Second, has at least one question type moved from cannot start to can start, which is the only realistic four-week gain and is more honest than a mark? Third, do the artefacts exist? If all three hold, continue and book the pre-exam home sessions. If two hold, continue for four more weeks with one specific thing fixed in writing.

Stop signals are worth naming in advance so you recognise them rather than explain them away. At two weeks: no written note has arrived, or the plan changes every session, or the tutor has not asked to see a single piece of marked school work. At four weeks: your child cannot say what the sessions are for, nothing has been marked against criteria, or the homework set is never checked the following week. Any one of those is grounds to stop. Tell us, and we move you to the next tutor on the shortlist with the plan and the artefacts handed over, so the new person starts at week five rather than week one. Changing tutors at four weeks costs a month. Changing at four months costs a grade.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks, expect a change in behaviour and not a change in grade. The realistic markers are that your child can start a question type she previously skipped, that she can say what the criteria reward in a piece of coursework, and that she has a folder with marked work in it. Marks at this stage move for reasons that have nothing to do with tutoring, including which topic the test happened to cover, so treating a test score as the four-week verdict is how families fire a tutor who was working and keep one who was not.

At one term, roughly a June start assessed in October, you should see the gap between school test performance and homework performance narrowing, fewer topics the student flatly avoids, and coursework drafts arriving before deadlines instead of during them. For a DP student the clearest signal is IA progress: a draft that exists, has been read, and has been revised once. For an IGCSE student it is past-paper work where method marks are being picked up even when the final answer is wrong, which is the thing Extended Mathematics candidates most often leave on the table.

At one exam cycle, you can finally judge the paper technique: timing, question selection, how the student handles the long-response items, whether she wrote anything at all on the parts she found hard. That is a year of work, and it is the first point at which a grade is a fair measure of anything. There is no single best IB and IGCSE tutor in Vasai, and no tutor reaches a grade on her own; the student's own hours, the school's teaching and the subject combination all sit inside the result.

Which is why we will not promise you an outcome. We do not guarantee grades, and any tutor who does is selling you something they cannot know. What we will do is tell you when a match is not working before you have paid for a term of it, hand the next tutor the plan and the artefacts so no time is lost, and say plainly when the problem is not tutoring at all. Sometimes the honest answer in this belt is that the commute is eating the study hours, and the fix is a schedule change rather than another subject specialist.

sections.heading: Getting started with an IB and IGCSE tutor in Vasai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Four things make the first shortlist good instead of generic. The school name and the year group. The exact subjects with levels, so HL, SL, Core or Extended is stated rather than guessed. The last two pieces of marked school work, including the bad one, because that tells a tutor more in thirty seconds than a paragraph of description does. And your two workable weekday evening slots plus one weekend slot, which is what makes a Saturday block of home classes possible later.

If there is a deadline in the next month, say so first. An IA draft due in three weeks, a mock on a known date, a subject the school has flagged: those change the shortlist and change what the first session does. A tutor walking into a three-week IA deadline runs a different first session than one starting a June-to-March engagement, and conflating the two wastes the only session where diagnosis is cheap.

The first session is diagnostic, and it should end with something written. The tutor works through the marked paper you supplied, identifies what broke, names the syllabus sections involved, and sets one task for the next forty-eight hours. You should receive a short note the same evening. That note is the first of the artefacts the four-week checkpoint depends on, so if it does not arrive, ask for it in week one rather than week three.

One last thing, said plainly because many families here hope otherwise: there is rarely one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents can book and forget. Two tutors who each own their half, with a written plan and a four-week checkpoint, is the arrangement that actually survives a Vasai academic year.

faqs.question: Can you actually find a weekday home tutor in Vasai, or is online the only real option?
faqs.answer: We can sometimes, but we will not pretend it is easy. Vasai is a forty-minute train ride north of Borivali, and the subject specialists who teach DP Physics or Extended IGCSE Mathematics mostly live south of the creek, so a weekday evening round trip costs them three hours for one lesson. Those arrangements usually lapse around week six. What holds is weekly online lessons with the right specialist plus in-person home classes booked in advance for the weeks before mocks, ideally on a Saturday. If you are in Vasai West or Vasai East and your subject is widely taught, a weekly local home tutor is worth trying first.

faqs.question: What should I ask in a trial session if I cannot meet the tutor in person?
faqs.answer: Ask her to teach the topic your child failed most recently, and hand over the marked paper rather than describing it. Then judge four things: whether the first ten minutes are spent diagnosing instead of lecturing, whether she names the syllabus section and the mark scheme, whether your child does most of the writing, and whether the session ends with one specific task for the next forty-eight hours. Also ask her directly what would make her tell you this is not working. A session where your child happily watched a confident adult solve everything beautifully is a bad session, however good it felt at the time.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Vasai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level first, then subject scarcity, then travel, then session length. DP Higher Level work costs more per hour than MYP support because the pool of people who can teach it is smaller. Scarce subjects, Further Mathematics, Economics HL, second-language work, sit above common ones for the same reason. Travel is a real factor here: a tutor crossing the creek for a weekday evening lesson is paying for three hours of her day, and that shows up in the rate or in the arrangement quietly ending. Online removes most of the travel component. We will not quote a figure on a page, because it would be wrong for half the people reading it.

faqs.question: Our tutor travels from Borivali. What happens when the trains are disrupted?
faqs.answer: Agree the fallback before you need it, in week one. The rule that works is simple: if the tutor cannot reach Vasai Road, the session runs online at the same time rather than being cancelled, and the cancellation only happens if neither side can get to a screen. Monsoon weeks on the Western Line will test this two or three times a term, more often than anywhere else in Mumbai we place tutors, and families who have not agreed it in advance lose the sessions. Make sure the shared whiteboard and the link are already set up and tested, because arranging that for the first time at 6pm on a disrupted evening does not work.

faqs.question: Do tutors come into the building, and what does our gate need?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the gate is usually a five-minute problem solved once. Give your security desk the tutor's name and a standing weekly slot in the visitors register rather than calling it in each week, and send the tutor the building name, wing and flat number along with the nearest landmark from Vasai Road, because addresses in the belt are often easier to find by landmark than by street. If your building requires a photo identity entry, tell the tutor to carry the same identity document we verified. For a weekly home tuition arrangement, a standing entry saves ten minutes of every session over a term.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during a home session?
faqs.answer: For younger children yes, for DP students usually not, but somebody adult should be in the flat. For PYP and MYP students an adult nearby keeps the session on track and gives you a direct sense of how the teaching works, which is valuable in the first month. For DP and IGCSE students an adult hovering is counterproductive. What matters more than supervision is the space: a table rather than a bed, a chair at the right height, the phone in another room, and the television off. A home tutor who asks you to change the study space in the first fortnight is doing her job, not being difficult.

faqs.question: It is four weeks in and I see no progress. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Hold the checkpoint conversation rather than waiting another month. Three questions decide it. Can your child say what she is working on this week and why, without looking it up? Has one question type moved from cannot start to can start? Do the artefacts exist, meaning session notes, a topic plan and at least two pieces of her own work marked against criteria? If all three hold, continue, because four weeks is too early for marks to move. If two hold, continue for four more weeks with one specific thing fixed in writing. If one or none hold, tell us and we move you on.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for Maths and Physics?
faqs.answer: It works well for algebra, graph work, data response and anything with a document or diagram at the centre, and less well for handwritten multi-step working. The difference is the handwriting channel. A tutor writing on a tablet into a shared whiteboard, with the student photographing her own working and dropping it in, gets close to in-person quality. A tutor talking over a static screen while the student writes unseen does not. So ask specifically how handwriting is shared before you book Mathematics or Physics online. For a DP Economics commentary or an English coursework draft, online loses almost nothing.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we move you, and the handover matters more than the speed. We ask for the specific reason, because it changes who comes next: a tutor who is kind but not rigorous needs replacing with someone different from a tutor who is rigorous but cannot hold a teenager's attention. The next tutor receives the topic plan, the marked work and the session notes from the trial month, so she starts at week five rather than week one. There is no requirement to persist with a bad match out of politeness. Changing tutors at four weeks costs a month; changing at four months costs a grade.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both my children if one is in MYP and one in DP?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and only within a subject family. A strong Mathematics specialist can usually hold MYP Mathematics and DP Mathematics Applications and Interpretation SL in the same evening, and that doubles up well on travel if she is coming to Vasai in person. Across subject families it rarely works: the person who teaches MYP Individuals and Societies criteria well is not normally the person who teaches DP Physics HL. If you need both, book two tutors and stagger them on different evenings, rather than asking one person to cover ground she will handle at only one end.

faqs.question: Should we add in-person home sessions before mocks, and when do we book them?
faqs.answer: Yes, and book them in October or November for a January mock, not in January. In-person home classes earn their travel most during revision, when the work is paper technique: timing a full paper, choosing which long-response question to attempt, and seeing where the student stops writing. A tutor sitting next to her can catch all of that in one sitting. Book the block in writing at the start of the engagement, specify weekend slots so the travel across the creek is survivable, and accept that a weekday 6pm pre-mock session from Borivali will be the one that gets cancelled.

faqs.question: Should we ask for online sessions to be recorded?
faqs.answer: Ask what the tutor's practice is, and decide with your child rather than for her. Recordings are genuinely useful for dense content subjects, where a DP student can rewatch a derivation during revision, and for the first fortnight when you are still judging the teaching. They are less useful for discussion-heavy sessions, where being recorded makes a nervous student quieter and less likely to admit she is lost. Whatever you agree, agree it explicitly at the start, including who keeps the files and for how long. Do not record without telling the tutor, and do not let a recording replace the written session note.

vasant-vihar-thane.heroIntro: An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Vasant Vihar, Thane is usually booked for one reason: the colony sits a short walk from the school corridor on Pokhran Road No 2, and parents want teaching to start minutes after the bell. sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP or IGCSE: which programme does your Mumbai school actually run?
paragraphs: Start with the label on the report card, because the word IB covers four different animals. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the junior years and is assessed by the teacher rather than an external board. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years and marks every subject against published criteria A to D. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year sixth-form course with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects, an Internal Assessment (IA) in each, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). Cambridge IGCSE is a separate qualification from Cambridge International Education sat at the end of Year 11, with Pearson Edexcel International GCSE running a parallel route at some Mumbai schools.

Families in this colony sit across all of these, because the two schools most used here follow different pathways. That matters for an after-school slot more than it first looks. A PYP child at a quarter to five is a completely different proposition from a DP1 student: the younger one can do thirty focused minutes and then needs to move, while the older one can work for ninety if the hour is sequenced properly and will simply stall if it is not. Booking an IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai without naming the programme usually produces somebody who teaches the content competently and the assessment style badly, which is the kind of mismatch that only shows up when the first marked task comes back.

The practical consequence is that one household often needs two arrangements rather than one. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is an accurate description of the pool, not of any individual: the person who handles MYP Sciences criteria is rarely the same person who prepares DP Economics IAs against the published bands. Where two children in the same flat need help, we usually stagger them instead of running a shared session. The younger child takes the early slot while the appetite for work still exists, and the older one takes the later slot after food, a shower and a genuine break from being instructed by adults.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended: the decisions behind the booking
paragraphs: Most parents call about a subject and are really calling about a decision. In Cambridge IGCSE the first one is tier. Mathematics 0580, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 and most Sciences are entered at Core or Extended, and the Core tier caps the top grade available. A child pushed into Extended to protect future options can spend a year dropping marks on questions the Core paper would never have asked, while a child parked in Core to keep things calm can find a DP Science pathway closed two years later. A tutor who has prepared students for both tiers will tell you which side of that line the child is on after three or four marked past-paper questions, not after a term of lessons.

In the Diploma Programme the equivalent decision is Higher Level against Standard Level, taken alongside the six subject groups and the Core. Higher Level adds content, an additional option topic and a longer paper, and it raises the expectation of independent handling in the Internal Assessment even though the criteria themselves are shared with Standard Level. Every DP subject carries an IA: a Mathematics exploration, a scientific investigation, a Business Management research project, an oral in Language and Literature. All of it is drafted during term time on top of ordinary teaching, which is why the school calendar matters as much as the syllabus when you decide which month to start.

Covering all IB and IGCSE subjects through home classes in Vasant Vihar, Thane does not mean one tutor covers everything. It means the pool is wide enough that a Year 9 needing MYP Mathematics support and a DP2 needing Chemistry Higher Level help are both matched, almost always to different people. Languages and the smaller Group 6 subjects are the scarce end of that pool. A DP Visual Arts or French B request takes longer to fill than Physics, and a family who needs it on a weekday evening will usually take the first genuinely good tutor and build the week around them, rather than holding out for a slot that was never going to appear.

The trade-off is travel: home tuition is only ever as reliable as the tutor's own commute, which is why the local match matters more than the glossier profile from across Mumbai.

Online works better than many Thane parents expect, and it works best in two specific situations. The first is a scarce subject. Against that: a tired twelve-year-old on a video call is harder to keep honest, and handwriting-heavy working is harder to watch as it happens.

Hybrid is where most households in this colony land by the second term. The straight-after-school weekday session stays at home, because that is the hour that needs a human in the room keeping a tired child on task. The second weekly session moves online to a later time: a forty-minute check on the week's work, a marked past paper walked through on screen, a quick look at an IA draft. It also gives the arrangement somewhere to go when the tutor is held up in traffic, so the default becomes a changed format rather than a cancelled hour.

sections.heading: How is a tutor checked before they teach in your flat?
paragraphs: Every tutor is identity-checked and qualification-checked before a profile becomes visible, and the board claim is checked separately from the degree. A Physics postgraduate qualification is not evidence that somebody has taught Cambridge IGCSE 0625 or DP Physics Standard Level. What counts is whether they can describe the paper structure, use the command terms correctly and say where students usually lose marks. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Vasant Vihar, Thane who has taken students through a full exam cycle on your board is worth more to you than a more decorated tutor who has not, and we weight the shortlist that way deliberately.

Somebody who has been teaching in Pokhran Road and Thane West at fixed hours for a couple of years is a known quantity on this corridor, and reliability at a quarter to five is a harder qualification to fake than a subject claim. Where a tutor is new to the platform we start them on slots that do not depend on a long evening drive, because a late arrival on a straight-after-school booking does more damage than it would at eight in the evening, when the child is at the table anyway.

Do your own checking in the first session, and do it on the work rather than on the person. Ask the tutor to mark one answer from your child's last school paper in front of you and explain the mark scheme wording they are applying. Ask which component the child's weakest topic appears in. Ask what they intend to do in the first twenty minutes of a quarter-to-five session with a child who has not eaten since lunch. A tutor who answers those three questions precisely is the one to book. A tutor who answers with warm generalities about potential and confidence is not, however pleasant the conversation feels.

sections.heading: What does a 4.45pm home tuition session in Vasant Vihar, Thane actually look like?
paragraphs: It starts with food and a clock, not with a textbook. A session beginning fifteen minutes after the school bell meets a child who has been awake since early morning, last ate at lunch, and has had no gap at all between being directed by adults at school and being directed by an adult at home. Everything that goes wrong in this slot goes wrong because somebody ignored that and opened with new content.

The shape that works on this corridor is predictable: ten minutes of eating and nothing else, then fifteen to twenty minutes of low-cost retrieval, then the hardest block while the food is doing its job, then a short closing task that finishes inside the hour. The low-cost opening is not filler. Recalling definitions, balancing a few equations, stating the units for a quantity, running through short-answer questions the child has already seen once: these cost very little concentration and pull the student back into the subject. Teaching something genuinely new in the first ten minutes is where most straight-after-school arrangements quietly fail, and the parent usually blames the tutor when the real fault is the running order.

Take a Year 11 student at Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School sitting Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620. Paper 6, the alternative to practical, suits a quarter-to-five slot almost perfectly: reading a burette scale, tabulating results to a consistent number of decimal places, plotting a line of best fit, identifying the variable that should have been controlled, writing the one-line conclusion the mark scheme is waiting for. It is precise, bounded work with immediate feedback, and a tired student can do it genuinely well. The same student's Paper 4 extended questions on moles and titration calculations are the opposite: multi-step reasoning where a slip in step two stays invisible until the final answer comes out wrong. Those belong at half past six after a real break, or on a Saturday morning.

The same test applies in the Diploma Programme. A DP2 student working on a Biology Higher Level Internal Assessment, choosing a statistical test and arguing why the sample size is defensible, should not be attempting it at a quarter to five on a Wednesday. That is open-ended independent thinking and it needs a brain with something left in it. An unseen English Literature extract is the same story, and so is a first TOK essay plan. The honest answer to can you come straight after school is therefore sometimes no, or not for this piece of work, and a tutor who takes the early hour because it is free and then spends it on exactly the wrong task has wasted the one slot the family was protecting.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at marks. Look at whether the child can say what they are being assessed on. The honest four-week markers are smaller than parents hope: homework being started without an argument, fewer blank openings on structured questions, the child using command terms correctly in ordinary conversation about the subject. Anybody promising a visible grade jump inside a month on a Cambridge IGCSE subject is telling you what you want to hear, and on this corridor that promise is usually followed by a tutor who starts arriving late once the novelty has worn off.

One term in, a marked school assessment gives the first real signal, and it should be read as a direction rather than a verdict. The useful question is where the marks moved. Method marks recovered in Mathematics 0580 structured questions, or evaluation marks picked up in the final part of a Sciences question, matter more than a flat percentage because they point to a specific repair that can be repeated. A term is also long enough to judge the slot itself. If the child is still flat at a quarter to five after eight weeks of sensible sessions, the hour is wrong rather than the tutor, and moving it is cheaper than starting again.

Across a full exam cycle you see the thing you were actually paying for: performance under timed conditions that stops surprising everybody. And here is the limit, stated plainly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor can. What a good arrangement reliably produces is a student who knows the structure of every paper, has worked each component against the clock, and has fewer topics they avoid looking at. The rest depends on what the child does in the other hours of the week. Any tutor in Mumbai who offers a guaranteed grade should be treated with real scepticism, whatever their results sheet claims.

When it is not working, say so early rather than waiting for the term to end. The most common pattern on this corridor is a tutor who is academically strong and cannot hold attention at this particular hour, which is a scheduling fault at least as often as a teaching one. We will usually try the slot change first, because moving a session from a quarter to five to half past six repairs more arrangements than swapping tutors does. If that does not work we match again from the same pool with the reason recorded, so the next tutor starts with information instead of a blank page.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Vasant Vihar, Thane depend on?
faqs.answer: They depend on five things, and an honest figure does not exist in the abstract. Board and level come first, because the pool of tutors who can prepare a Diploma Programme Higher Level subject and mark against its criteria is smaller than the pool for middle-school support. Subject scarcity comes next: Physics and Maths are easier to fill than French B. Travel is third, and it is the one families here can influence, since a tutor coming down the Ghodbunder stretch or across from Mulund West prices that commute in. Session length and weekly frequency complete the calculation, and a longer session is rarely priced as a simple multiple of a shorter one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor really reach my building within fifteen minutes of the school bell?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor already works on this side of Thane. Somebody teaching in Pokhran Road, Thane West or Hiranandani Estate Thane earlier in the afternoon can reach a lane in this colony in minutes, because Vasant Vihar sits beside the school corridor on Pokhran Road No 2. A tutor travelling in from Kasarvadavali down Ghodbunder Road in the evening cannot, whatever they say in the first call. We filter for this before you ever see a profile, and we would rather offer you an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Vasant Vihar, Thane at half past six than a quarter-to-five slot that slips every single week.

faqs.question: Is a quarter to five too early for a Diploma Programme student?
faqs.answer: No, provided the work matches the hour. A DP student uses an early session well for past-paper questions, marked work walked through, definitions, and problem sets with short feedback loops. What they should not be doing at that hour is drafting an Internal Assessment or planning a Theory of Knowledge essay, because open-ended writing needs a brain that has rested and eaten. Several DP2 families in this colony run one early weekday session for drilling and keep the thinking work for a Saturday morning. That is a better use of both hours than forcing everything into whichever slot happens to be free.

faqs.question: My child is exhausted after school. Should we book an evening slot instead?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and a good tutor will suggest it before you do. If your child is genuinely flat at a quarter to five after a fair trial, move the session to half past six and protect the gap for food, a shower and nothing in particular. The early slot is popular in Vasant Vihar, Thane because the colony sits beside the school corridor and the child is home very early, not because early is better. The counter-argument is bedtime: a late session that pushes homework to ten at night costs a Year 9 or Year 10 student more than it gains.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is stuck in traffic on Ghodbunder Road?
faqs.answer: The session moves online for that day instead of being cancelled. Ghodbunder Road in the evening is the single most common reason a Thane session slips, and a tutor who already has a shared document and a camera set up can run the planned hour from wherever they are. We ask tutors to tell the family by a clear cut-off time rather than at the door. If a tutor is repeatedly late, treat it as a matching error on our side: we will change the slot or the tutor, because an unreliable hour is worse for a child than no hour at all.

faqs.question: Does online tuition actually work for Cambridge IGCSE Maths?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one condition: the student has to write where the tutor can see it. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is marked on method, so a session where the tutor only sees final answers is close to useless. A document camera, a tablet, or a phone propped over the page solves it completely. Online suits revision, worked solutions and past-paper walkthroughs, and suits a drifting Year 9 less well. Plenty of families in this colony keep Maths at home and run a second online session for something scarcer, such as Economics or a second language.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the diagnostic to be repeated before changing anything. Four weeks is long enough to see habits change, not marks, so check the smaller signals first: is homework being started, are structured questions no longer left blank, is the child using command terms correctly. If those signals are missing too, the arrangement is wrong rather than the timeline. The two usual causes are the slot and the diagnosis: a child being taught at the wrong hour, or a tutor working on the topic the parent named instead of the component where the marks are actually leaking away.

faqs.question: How does a replacement work if the tutor is not right for us?
faqs.answer: You tell us, and we match again from the same pool with the reason recorded. There is no argument about it and no notice period beyond paying for sessions already taught. Before changing the tutor we will usually suggest changing the hour, because on this corridor a mismatch at a quarter to five is often a tiredness problem wearing the costume of a teaching problem. If the reason is academic, for instance a tutor who knows the subject but not the Cambridge IGCSE paper structure, we will say that plainly and match for board experience next time.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: No, but an adult should be in the flat. Most tutors prefer a parent at home for the first two or three sessions, after which the arrangement runs on its own. You do not need to sit in the room, and a parent listening from the next room usually gets a more honest session than one supervising from the next chair. What helps far more is being available for five minutes at the end, so the tutor can say what was covered and what the homework is before leaving for their next stop in Thane West or Pokhran Road.

faqs.question: What happens to a missed session during the February exam run?
faqs.answer: Tell the tutor as early as you can and ask for the hour to be moved rather than written off. During the run of Cambridge written papers from late February, schools add revision classes and practicals at short notice and a fixed weekly slot will collide at least once. Most tutors will swap to a weekend morning that week, which is usually better anyway because exam-period work is long-form practice under time. A session cancelled on the day with no notice is normally chargeable, and that is fair: the tutor has already given up the travel window.

faqs.question: What should the search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Vasant Vihar, Thane actually mean?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a search phrase rather than a category. There is no ranked list of tutors in this colony, and anybody publishing one is selling placement. What parents mean when they type it is a tutor who knows their child's board, can hold the exact hour they need every week, and will say honestly when a different slot or a different subject specialist would serve the child better. Judge a tutor on one marked past paper, a clear diagnosis of where the marks are going, and three weeks of punctuality on Pokhran Road. Adjectives are not evidence.

They are there to establish what the student can already do unaided, where the marks are leaking, and whether the two of them can work for an hour without a parent refereeing from the next room. You hear the tutor's honest read on all three afterwards, including the uncomfortable parts.

After that you confirm, ask for a different tutor, or stop. There is no package to buy up front and no term you are committed to. If you confirm, the slot becomes a standing weekly booking, the tutor obtains whatever visitor or gate clearance your building in Vashi requires, and the first four sessions are treated as a trial of the match rather than a settled arrangement. Most tutor changes happen inside that window, and asking for one is routine rather than awkward.
